name: Compare Project Judgment Stats 2 Plan
description: Add adjudicated conflict-resolution truth stats to the Compare Project Judgments page without changing judgment data, with resolved-only truth metrics and clearly labeled fallback behavior.

userStories.title: Add resolved-only human conflict-resolution stats kind
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a dedicated Human vs conflict-resolution stats kind so adjudicated truth metrics do not reuse the existing fallback conflict-resolution behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a server comparison kind such as `human-vs-conflict-resolution` for `Human vs After conflict resolution (resolved only)`.
Include the new comparison only when conflict resolution is enabled and the page is in summary mode.
For the in-memory helper path, include only articles where saved conflict resolution and Human each have one valid binary decision.
For the new comparison, do not fall back to Human when saved conflict resolution is missing or non-binary.
For the new comparison, `Overlap` is the resolved-only denominator used by the row's counts and rates.
For the new comparison, `Cohen's Kappa`, `Sensitivity`, and `Specificity` use conflict resolution as truth and Human as prediction.
Existing Human vs LLM, LLM vs LLM, and LLM vs After conflict resolution group generation remains unchanged.
`bun test src/server/routes/comparisonProjectsRoutes/comparisonProjectStats.test.ts` passes
`bun test src/server/routes/ComparisonProjectsRoutes.rollback.test.ts` passes
`bun run lint` passes
`bun run build` passes
`bun run desktop:build` passes

userStories.title: Compute resolved-only conflict-resolution stats in SQL
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the production SQL aggregate path to compute the same resolved-only Human vs conflict-resolution metrics as the in-memory helper path.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `getComparisonProjectStatsAggregatesSql` to produce the `human-vs-conflict-resolution` row using saved conflict resolution answers only.
The SQL path excludes unresolved articles, non-binary conflict-resolution answers, and Human answers that are missing or non-binary for the new row.
The SQL path computes `Overlap`, conflicts, true conflicts, kappa, sensitivity, and specificity with the same resolved-only denominator as the in-memory helper path.
The existing `llm-vs-conflict-resolution` SQL fallback behavior is preserved for post-resolution fallback rows.
Tests cover SQL/helper parity for counts, kappa, sensitivity, specificity, missing resolution exclusion, and non-binary resolution exclusion.
`bun test src/server/routes/comparisonProjectsRoutes/comparisonProjectStats.test.ts` passes
`bun test src/server/routes/ComparisonProjectsRoutes.rollback.test.ts` passes
`bun run lint` passes
`bun run build` passes
`bun run desktop:build` passes

userStories.title: Clarify main project stats conflict-resolution rows
userStories.description: As a user, I want the main Project Stats table to make resolved-only rows and fallback rows visually clear so I know which denominator and truth source each row uses.
acceptanceCriteria: Show the new row as `Human vs After conflict resolution (resolved only)` in the current `Project Stats` table.
Label existing `LLM vs After conflict resolution` rows as `post-resolution fallback` without changing their fallback behavior.
Update the table description so each `After conflict resolution` row explains whether it is resolved-only or post-resolution fallback.
Keep the main table columns unchanged: `Comparison`, `Column Info`, `Overlap`, `Conflicts`, `True Conflicts`, `Cohen's Kappa`, `Sensitivity`, `Specificity`.
The main table still renders existing Human vs LLM and LLM vs LLM rows with no behavior change.

`bun test src/server/routes/ComparisonProjectsRoutes.rollback.test.ts` passes

`bun run build` passes
`bun run desktop:build` passes

userStories.title: Add resolved-only head-to-head stats backend
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want backend stats that compare Human and each LLM against saved conflict-resolution truth so the UI can show adjudicated head-to-head results.
acceptanceCriteria: Add backend response data for an `Additional Project Stats` resolved-only truth comparison section.
Return one head-to-head row per LLM, with each LLM using its own denominator: rows where Human, that LLM, and saved conflict resolution all have one valid binary decision.
Return `Resolved count`, `Human correct vs truth`, `Human errors vs truth`, `LLM correct vs truth`, `LLM errors vs truth`, and `Winner` for each LLM row.
Return `Both correct`, `Both wrong`, `Human only correct`, `LLM only correct`, and `LLM advantage` for each LLM row.
Compute confusion matrix metrics against conflict resolution truth: accuracy, balanced accuracy, precision, NPV, F1, truth prevalence, true correct, and true errors.
Return `N/A`-ready null values for rates when a denominator is zero, including McNemar chi-square when `LLM only correct + Human only correct = 0`.
Tests prove unresolved rows and non-binary rows do not affect head-to-head results.
`bun test src/server/routes/comparisonProjectsRoutes/comparisonProjectStats.test.ts` passes
`bun test src/server/routes/ComparisonProjectsRoutes.rollback.test.ts` passes
`bun run lint` passes
`bun run build` passes
`bun run desktop:build` passes

userStories.title: Render additional project stats section
userStories.description: As a user, I want an expandable Additional Project Stats section so I can compare Human and LLM performance against adjudicated truth without cluttering the main table.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an expandable `Additional Project Stats` section below the current stats table.
Add a `Resolved-only truth comparison` subsection that renders one row per LLM from the backend head-to-head stats.

Show `Resolved count`, `Human correct vs truth`, `Human errors vs truth`, `LLM correct vs truth`, `LLM errors vs truth`, `Winner`, `Both correct`, `Both wrong`, `Human only correct`, `LLM only correct`, and `LLM advantage`.
Show simple labels and short help text for additional metrics, including confusion matrix metrics and McNemar chi-square.
Display `N/A` when a metric denominator is zero or the backend value is null.
Keep headers, table shell, and loading/error handling consistent with the existing `Project Stats` card on browser and desktop flows.
